observations.text: Re-review delta at commit 866a873. ARGV: git diff --stat 191f376 866a873; exit 0; stdout: tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs (+49), tests/acceptance/support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs (+3) and the feature docs and run records. No production file changed in this delta. The delta is one new journey a_new_scan_accounts_for_its_own_repos_only, the constant PRIYA_CHOICE_OF_TWO = [TIDEPOOL, QUILL_DOCS], which is the three-repo choice with kelp unticked as the scenario says, the generalised wording of the shared count message, and one NotTested acceptance row for E2. Because the support change compiles into every review-app target, ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --no-run; exit 0; all 22 test executables built. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 10 passed, 0 failed in 6.41 s. Tree clean at 866a873.

I observed the E4 RED myself, with a mutation of the count alone. Mutation: in crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs the read-count subquery of LATEST_SCAN lost its planned.run_id = scan_runs.run_id predicate, so it counts every read row of the owner instead of the rows of her latest run; the planned-count discriminator was left intact. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 101; 5 passed, 5 failed in 6.12 s. a_new_scan_accounts_for_its_own_repos_only fails at left 5, right 2 - her queue claiming the five repos her two scans read between them where the scan she is looking at read two - which is exactly the over-count E4 names. The four older journeys catch the same mutation at left 4, 6, 5 and 5 against right 3, so the per-scan scope of the count is observed several times over and this journey is the one that isolates it. Restored with git checkout --; no proptest regression file was written and none remains; git status --porcelain empty; ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 10 passed in 6.51 s.

The new journey is a public observation and reuses what already exists. It drives the real binary over HTTP: her first scan of three repos completes and its queue count is asserted, she then saves a choice of two and scans again, and the journey asserts that the second scan read exactly the two repos she had chosen by then, that it ended completed, and that her queue carries exactly one repos-read line reading two. It reuses given_scanned, when_scans, show_repos_read, show_queue_evidence, then_the_run_ended and the shared then_her_queue_accounts_for_the_whole_scan rather than adding a parallel assertion, and that shared helper's generalised WHAT/WHY/HOW still names what failed, why it matters to her and what must become true, now also covering a count that names repos of a scan before this one.

The NotTested E2 row is honest, correctly owned and leaves no promised outcome unobserved. Its claim that no public path reaches a run that saved a read and was then interrupted checks out against the fault vocabulary: the development binary parses exactly migrate_before_commit, refuse_mark_repo_read and refuse_record_account_checks (crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:313-315), the mark fault refuses every mark so such a run saves nothing, the other fires before any repo is read, and the restart sweep marks only a running run interrupted. Reaching that state needs a new fault name that refuses the second and later marks, which is a declaration of the store fault seam and belongs to ADR-091, the owner the row names, not to the oracle. The substance of E2 is already observed: in a_run_cut_short_keeps_what_it_saved_and_the_run_after_it_reads_only_the_rest the run that is picked up ends interrupted while its plan carries a read saved earlier in the scan, and the run after it still accounts for three; production's resume path does not distinguish an interrupted run from a rate-limited one (resumes_frozen_plan) and L1/F101 holds over any frozen plan whatever stopped it. What is uncovered is only which run made the saved mark, which the count cannot see, since it counts rows of the latest plan and not the run that marked them. No finding; the open question is the ADR owner's to answer.

Closure and budgets after this delta: ten executable observations bind P1 and P2 - five journeys over the real binary (one pause, two pauses, a cut-short run, re-read repos, and a new scan counting its own plan), three domain properties, the architectural check and the existing adapter purge test - plus one NotTested row owned by ADR-091. No obligation of the manifest is left without a falsifier and no test repeats another's observation. Timing: 6.41 s, 6.12 s and 6.51 s wall for 10 tests of which five drive the real binary over HTTP, the share ADR-091 accepts for this family and far below the 300 s suite ceiling; nothing sits near half of its own budget, so no nine-run median evidence was collected. typesafe: unavailable, carried from the probe recorded this session (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this process environment); every judgment here is locally derived from the measured runs and the read bytes.

diagnostic: Accepted, with no finding open. The E4 gap is closed by a public journey: her first scan of three repos completes, she unticks one and scans again, and her queue says two repos read, not the five her two scans read between them. I observed its RED myself by dropping the run_id predicate from the read-count subquery of LATEST_SCAN alone - left 5, right 2, the exact over-count E4 names - and the four older journeys caught the same mutation at left 4, 6, 5 and 5 against right 3, so the per-scan scope of the count is now observed several times over; after restoring the adapter the suite is green again at 10 passed, with the tree clean and no regression file. The new constant is the three-repo choice with one repo unticked, as the scenario says, and the generalised count message still names what failed, why it matters to her and what must become true. The NotTested E2 row is honest and correctly owned: the development binary parses only three fault names, the mark fault refuses every mark so no run can save a read and then be interrupted, and reaching that state needs a new fault name, which is a declaration of the store fault seam owned by ADR-091 rather than an oracle change - while the substance of E2 is already observed by the cut-short journey, whose interrupted run carries an earlier saved read into a plan the run after it still counts as three. Because the support change compiles into every review-app target, all 22 test executables were built. No design, implementation or product finding; nothing in this delta blocks completion.
